target.title: [AI-assisted] feat(android): add chat command controls
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: The Android chat surface did not give users an obvious new-chat/session-reset control or an in-composer slash command picker, leaving common chat actions hidden behind text-only behavior.
- Solution: Add Android chat controls for starting a new chat and discovering/selecting slash commands from the composer.
- What changed:
  - Added Android chat command metadata and command-list refresh plumbing.
  - Added a reusable slash-command matching/completion helper.
  - Added chat header/composer controls for new chat and slash command selection.
  - Intercepted `/new` and `/reset` locally so they start a fresh chat instead of sending a normal chat turn.
  - Added focused Android unit coverage for new-chat handling and slash command filtering.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Gateway command semantics, model routing, command execution, and provider behavior are unchanged. Slash suggestions intentionally match command names and aliases only, not description/category text.

## Motivation

- Android users should not need to guess hidden text commands for basic chat actions.
- The composer should expose the commands the Gateway already advertises, while keeping filtering predictable and avoiding noisy matches from descriptions or categories.

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- N/A (issue-less/team-approved Android app candidate)
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Android chat now has first-class controls for starting a new chat/session reset and selecting advertised slash commands from the composer. Slash filtering uses command name/alias prefixes only.
- Real environment tested (affected runtime/layer, not just "unit test"): Android app unit layer and Play debug APK build/install/launch path.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatCommandControlsTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerCommandControlsTest --console=plain --stacktrace
./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --console=plain --stacktrace
./gradlew :app:assemblePlayDebug --console=plain --stacktrace
```

- Evidence after fix:

```text
Focused Android unit tests: BUILD SUCCESSFUL
Full Android unit tests: BUILD SUCCESSFUL
Play debug APK assembly: BUILD SUCCESSFUL
Emulator smoke: Play debug APK installed and launched as ai.openclaw.app
```

- Public artifact URLs, if screenshots/videos/files are referenced:

```text
N/A
```

- Observed result after fix: Command filtering returns the expected command set for `/`, `/n`, `/mo`, `/de`, and does not match `/runtime` or `/session` through description/category text. New-chat slash handling starts a fresh chat path instead of sending the command as a normal chat message.
- What was not tested: A manual connected-Gateway chat session was not part of this verification.
- Before evidence:

```text
Android chat did not expose dedicated new-chat and slash-command controls in the composer/header surface.
```

- Remaining proof gap: None for the command filtering and new-chat handling covered by the targeted Android tests and APK build/smoke verification.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Android chat had chat send/history plumbing, but no first-class mobile control surface for common command discovery and new-chat/session-reset actions.
- Missing detection / guardrail: There was no focused Android test coverage locking slash command matching to command names/aliases or verifying local new-chat slash handling.
- Contributing context (if known): The Gateway already advertises command metadata, but Android did not expose it ergonomically in the chat composer.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file:
  - `ChatCommandControlsTest`
  - `ChatControllerCommandControlsTest`
- Scenario the test should lock in:
  - `/` lists commands.
  - Prefix queries match command names and aliases.
  - Description/category text does not create unrelated matches.
  - `/new` and `/reset` trigger a new-chat path.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The new behavior is mostly local Android command matching and composer/controller routing, so focused unit tests cover the risky logic without requiring a live Gateway.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): Existing Android chat controller tests covered adjacent chat behavior, but not these controls.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A; focused tests were added/updated.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Android chat users get visible controls for starting a new chat and selecting slash commands. Slash command suggestions are narrower and more predictable because they use name/alias prefix matching only.

## Diagram

```text
Gateway commands.list
        |
        v
Android ChatController / MainViewModel
        |
        v
Chat composer slash menu + new-chat controls
```

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No.
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No.
- New/changed network calls? No new endpoint; the Android app reuses existing Gateway command/chat surfaces.
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No command execution semantics changed; this is a UI/control surface over existing commands.
- Data access scope changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Android app test/build environment
- Runtime/container: Gradle Android test runner and Play debug APK build
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Android companion app chat surface
- Relevant config (redacted): N/A

### Steps

1. Run the focused Android command-control tests.
2. Run the full Android Play debug unit test suite.
3. Assemble the Play debug APK.
4. Install and launch the APK on an Android emulator smoke path.

### Expected

- Slash command matching stays limited to command names and aliases.
- New-chat slash commands trigger the new-chat path locally.
- Android unit tests and APK build pass.
- APK installs and launches.

### Actual

- Focused Android tests passed.
- Full Android unit tests passed.
- Play debug APK assembled successfully.
- APK installed and launched in the emulator.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

```text
:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatCommandControlsTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerCommandControlsTest -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL
:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL
:app:assemblePlayDebug -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL
```

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios:
  - Slash command filtering for all commands and prefix queries.
  - Alias-based matching for delegated command aliases.
  - No description/category match leakage for unrelated slash queries.
  - Local `/new` and `/reset` new-chat handling.
  - APK build/install/launch smoke.
- Edge cases checked:
  - Empty `/` query.
  - Prefix queries such as `/n`, `/mo`, and `/de`.
  - Non-command-matching queries such as `/runtime` and `/session`.
- What you did **not** verify: Manual connected-Gateway chat interaction.

## Review Conversations

- [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config/env changes? No.
- Migration needed? No.
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Android command suggestions could drift from Gateway command metadata.
  - Mitigation: The app reads advertised command metadata and falls back to a small default command set.
- Risk: Slash filtering could become noisy if it searches descriptive metadata.
  - Mitigation: Matching is limited to command name and aliases, with focused tests for that behavior.
